gizmo.title: Concept runner game
gizmo.description: A side scroller. The character runs on fire and never stops. Jump to grab the good concepts and over the bad ones, then see a recap of what was good and what was bad.

configure.title: Quest
configure.description: The prompt on the start screen.

configure.title: Concepts
configure.description: Good ones are grabbed, bad ones are jumped.

properties.title: Why it is good or bad
properties.description: Shown when the character meets it and again in the recap.

configure.title: Run length in seconds
configure.description: About how long the run lasts at normal speed.

configure.title: After the game
configure.description: Optional. Replaces the copy-a-prompt box on the finish panel with your own content, such as a next step or a link.

configure.title: Extra buttons after the game
configure.description: Optional. Buttons or links shown beside Play again on the finish panel.

advanced.title: Character seed
advanced.description: Any text. The same seed always makes the same character. This is the same seed the HAX avatar uses.

advanced.title: Use the signed in person's character
advanced.description: When someone is signed in to HAX, the character looks like their own avatar. Everyone else sees the seed above.

advanced.title: Passing score
advanced.description: A number from 0 to 1. Sent with the completed progress event as the success threshold.

advanced.title: Game name
advanced.description: Names this game in progress events and OER Schema markup.

advanced.title: Game id
advanced.description: Optional. Tells this game apart from others on the page in progress events.

items.label: Custom Elements
items.text: Define your own HTML tag with customElements.define. Browsers run this natively, so no library is needed.

items.label: React
items.text: A framework with its own runtime and build step. Its components are not browser features, so they need React everywhere they run.

items.label: Shadow DOM
items.text: Gives an element private markup and styles that the rest of the page cannot accidentally break.

items.label: TypeScript
items.text: Adds types, but browsers cannot run it. It has to be compiled to JavaScript before it ships.

items.label: HTML Templates
items.text: The template element holds markup that stays inert until you clone it, so it is cheap to define and reuse.

items.label: Angular
items.text: A full framework with its own compiler and template language. Its components need that toolchain and runtime to work.

items.label: Slots
items.text: Slots let authors drop their own content into an element, which is how one element can wrap anything.

items.label: JSX
items.text: Markup written inside JavaScript that browsers do not understand. It has to be compiled away first.

items.label: ES Modules
items.text: Native import and export load an element's code with no bundler in between.

items.label: jQuery
items.text: A library that smoothed over old browser differences. Most of what it did is now native, like querySelector and fetch.

items.label: ElementInternals
items.text: Lets a custom element join forms and expose accessibility roles and states through the browser itself.

items.label: Vue
items.text: Single file components need a compiler and the Vue runtime, so they are not plain browser code.

properties.prompt:
Quiz me on the web component standards so I remember what I just played. Use custom elements, shadow DOM, HTML templates, slots, ES modules and ElementInternals.

Ask one question at a time, wait for my answer, then tell me what I got right and what to review. After six questions, show me where each of them appears in a HAX element made with the HAX CLI (@haxtheweb/create).
properties.quest: Run through the web component specification. Jump to grab what is native web and over what is not.
properties.finishLead: Paste this into Claude to practice what you just ran.
